office_does: The three county commissioners set Franklin County's budget and taxes, maintain county roads and buildings, pass county ordinances and run the departments without an elected head.
race_blurb: Only District 3 voters choose between incumbent Clint Didier and planning commissioner Joel Prantle, both Republicans. Didier, who took 57.5% in the primary, runs on opposing any tax increase and limited government; Prantle runs on responsible growth and listening to constituents.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 3 commissioner and 2025 board chairman, a farmer running on no tax increases, private property rights and resisting state mandates.
highlights: 'I oppose any tax increases'; wants a government that 'lives within its means' [S1]
As chairman, ended the human services deal with Benton County over its cost in 2025 [S3]
Backed seeking the Attorney General opinion that former commissioners raised their own pay unconstitutionally [S4]
Says he started recording and preserving all commissioner meetings [S1]

taxes.basis: States flatly that he opposes any tax increase and campaigns for lower taxes.

spending.basis: Calls for government that lives within its means; record of ending a costly interlocal agreement and pursuing past commissioners' pay.

experience.basis: Sitting commissioner and 2025 chairman running on his record in office.

candidates.summary: Railway-supply business vice president and volunteer county planning commissioner, a 50-year resident running on responsible growth and listening to constituents.
highlights: Vice president of family-owned PF&S Railway Supply; volunteer planning commissioner [S1]
Promises 'responsible growth' and to make sure constituents' voices are heard [S1]
Describes himself as a conservative Republican who supports President Trump [S1]
Raised about $7,300, mostly from himself and family [S2][S3]

experience.basis: No elected record; challenges a sitting commissioner from a volunteer planning commission seat.
